comment: Path-scoped allowlist for scripts/secret-scan.php. Mirrored by .gitleaks.toml and .semgrepignore; tests/Unit/SecretScanTest.php fails when they differ. A new entry needs a reason of 20+ characters that says why the value is not a credential.

rules.reason: Golden-replay constants. Synthetic test values, not credentials: the signing key is derived from SHA-256 of the public string RivetIT-agent-TEST-seed (recomputed and matched in docs/security/CORE_SECURITY_AUDIT.md), the 8 enrollment secrets are one repeated character, the admin API token is the hex counting sequence. They exist only in scratch databases.

Byte-frozen cross-language protocol vectors (SHA256SUMS). Contain only the public TEST signing key (seed = SHA-256 of the public string RivetIT-agent-TEST-seed) and signatures made with it; verified to authenticate nothing outside the test suites. Not editable without breaking the freeze.
Frozen golden HTTP transcripts: hold only the public half of the TEST signing key (public keys are not secrets) and placeholder tokens.
Frozen original golden transcripts of the edition, same content class as golden/: public TEST key only.

Legacy ENC/ENC2/enc/vault/V1/V2 samples encrypted with fixture keys derived from public strings (settings key = SHA-256 of rivetcore-fixture-settings-key; the master key and password are the literals in generate.php). All 15 samples decrypt under those published keys to documented sample plaintexts; none was made with an installation key.
Envelope v3 known-answer vectors. The 32-byte key is the byte sequence 01..20 (hex counting), a published-style test key.
Generator of legacy_samples.json; fixed fixture secrets that are readable words or derived from public strings (see legacy_samples.json).
Known-answer test key: the byte sequence 01..20.
AES-256-GCM known-answer test: the McGrew and Viega GCM specification test case 16 key (feffe992...), a public specification vector.
Test cookie key: the byte sequence 00..1f followed by 0xff 0xee... (hex counting), never used outside this unit test.

Redactor tests must contain strings that LOOK like secrets: sequential or documented-example values (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE, a 38-character ghp_ string that fails GitHub's own length and CRC32 checksum, a 3-segment xoxb string, a JWT built at run time with a published fixture HMAC key). None authenticates anywhere.
Job output redaction test: same synthetic secret-looking strings as RedactorTest; the JWT is built at run time from a published fixture key.
Change-monitor redaction cases (bob:tok3n123@host, /p:pw1234): obviously fake 8-character credentials in a URL, to prove they are masked.
Wrong-password connection test: an explicit 'wrong' marker string that is rejected by design; no real server accepts it.
Seed string of five readable words for the golden-replay SecretBox key in a scratch database; not used anywhere else.
Redaction test echoes a ghp_-shaped string whose body is a contiguous alphabet run and whose CRC32 checksum is invalid, so it cannot be a GitHub token.
Redaction test: obviously fake PEM body (SECRETKEYBODYLINE2) and bob:tok3n123@host; no key material.
Rotated-credential round-trip test value (devtok_rotated_fixture).
Setup test enrollment token rvte1.selabc.fixturepart123: wrong shape for a real token (6-character selector, 13-character secret).
Same synthetic setup token as setup_test.go and the standard documentation UUID.
Mock build-host server test token (tok_fixture_build_host_value); the mock server accepts anything it is given by the test and nothing else.
Documents the public TEST signing key.
Documents the public TEST signing key.
Authentication helper tests use short throwaway strings such as tk_abc.DEF-123 and p:ss w0rd to exercise header validation; none is a credential.
Documentation: variable names such as $config_settings_enc_key, the public salt string rivetit-settings-key-fingerprint|v1| and the sample passphrase s3cret!; no key material.
Mock server test token (23 characters, readable words) accepted only by the in-test httptest server.
Installer-trailer test token rvte1.sel123.sEcReTsEcReT_-x: wrong shape for a real token (6-character selector, 15-character secret).
Vector generator: enrollment token whose secret is the hex counting sequence 0123456789abcdef...; written into frozen vector files only.
False positive: the asserted list of migration identifiers (0002_..., 0003_...) looks like an API key to entropy rules.
Change-monitor redaction cases: fake key=value lines (--key-file, user=alice) to prove masking.
Branch compliance (not yet on main): the profile codec rejects secrets in labels; the AWS-shaped value is an ascending alphabet filler, not a key.
Branch compliance (not yet on main): a description string flagged by entropy rules; a test label, not a credential.
Branch store-info (not yet on main): throwaway password constant for a scratch Postgres in a test.
The scanner's own regular expressions, placeholder words and examples.
